title: I Tested Every Weird Kitchen Gadget From the 90s
creator: Ruben Castillo
description:
I bought six kitchen gadgets from 90s infomercials off eBay and actually tried to cook with them. Some of them should have stayed in the 90s.

Instagram: @rubencooksthings
Business: hello@rubencastillo.tv

sentences.t: So I spent way too much money on eBay buying kitchen gadgets from nineties infomercials, and today we find out if any of them actually work.
Gadget number one, the egg cracker.
You put the egg in this little cage, squeeze the handles, and it's supposed to split the shell perfectly and drop the egg into the bowl.
Let's try it.
Okay, that's mostly shell, and a little bit of egg on my shirt.
Try two, gentler.
That worked, actually, that was kind of satisfying, but it's slower than just cracking an egg on the counter.
Gadget number two, the banana slicer, which is the one everyone made fun of on the internet.
And I have to say, it works perfectly, as long as your banana is shaped exactly like the slicer, which mine isn't.
Half the slices are perfect and the other half are still attached to each other.
Gadget three, the rotisserie oven, the one with the guy yelling set it and forget it.
I put a whole chicken in about an hour ago, and honestly, look at this.
That's a great chicken, the skin is crispy, it's juicy, I'm a little shocked.
Okay, I'll be honest, this video took a lot of eBay money, so it's sponsored by two companies, and here's the first one.
MeUndies makes the softest underwear I own, and I'm not just saying that because they're paying me.
They're made from this micromodal fabric that's stupidly comfortable, and they come in prints, including one with tiny tacos, which I'm wearing right now, probably.
You can get a pack, or do the membership and get a new pair every month.
Go to meundies.com/ruben for twenty percent off your first order and free shipping.
And sponsor number two is Skillshare.
Skillshare is an online learning community with thousands of classes taught by people who actually do the thing, cooking, photography, editing, illustration, whatever you're into.
I took a food photography class on there last year, and it's the reason my thumbnails stopped looking like crime scene photos.
The first five hundred people to use my link, skillshare.com/ruben, will get a one-month free trial.
Alright, gadget number four, the pasta maker that extrudes noodles out of the front like a Play-Doh factory.
You dump in flour, pour in water and egg, and it mixes and pushes out spaghetti.
It is loud, it is very loud, my neighbors probably think I'm drilling.
The pasta that came out is gummy and a little sad, but it is technically pasta.
Gadget five is the hamburger press with the little hole maker, so your patties don't puff up.
Honestly, that works great, and it's probably the only one I'll keep using.
And last, gadget number six, the electric can opener that's supposed to cut around the can by itself.
It walked about a quarter of the way around and then just spun in place making a sad noise.
Rest in peace.
So the final ranking, the rotisserie and the burger press are winners, the egg cracker and banana slicer are fine if you're bored, and the pasta maker and can opener go back on eBay.
Let me know what gadget from your childhood I should try next.
